tier-selection.summary: All tier selections justified via UCE34 Q10 analysis

justification.q10-analysis: Probabilistic membership testing for duplicate detection
justification.why-t10: - Approximate data structure (0.08% FPR acceptable) - Space efficiency (8KB for 10K items) - Speed (<30ns query, <50ns insert) - Skip 50-90% of MinHash computations (2-10× speedup)
justification.alternatives-considered: - HashSet: O(n) memory, exact but slower - T9 Persistent: Overkill for transient filter - Raw Bloom: Requires manual bit manipulation (error-prone)

justification.q10-analysis: High-throughput batch processing with parallel coordination
justification.why-t4: - Embarrassingly parallel (independent document processing) - Batch efficiency (amortize overhead across multiple docs) - Lockfree coordination (ThreadPool + LockfreeResultAggregator) - Target 576K docs/sec @ 16 cores (9.6× baseline)
justification.alternatives-considered: - Rayon: Requires Arc<Mutex> for result aggregation (contention) - Tokio async: Overhead for CPU-bound task (>100μs per doc) - Single-threaded: 60K docs/sec insufficient for 10M corpus

justification.q10-analysis: Runtime SIMD selection for portable performance
justification.why-t2: - Data parallelism (8-lane MinHash with f32x8) - Adaptive (detect AVX2/SSE4.2 at runtime) - Portable (universal scalar fallback) - Validated speedup (7.1× SIMD vs scalar)
justification.alternatives-considered: - Compile-time dispatch: Requires separate binaries (AVX2, SSE4.2, scalar) - Always-scalar: Misses 7.1× speedup opportunity - Always-SIMD: Crashes on non-AVX2 CPUs
